lead: Chesapeake is big, flat and low, with tidal rivers on one side and the Great Dismal Swamp on the other. Heavy rain, high water tables and nor'easters drive most of its water damage.
risk: heavy rain flooding, high groundwater and coastal storms
risk_short: heavy rain, high groundwater, coastal storms
why: Much of Chesapeake sits only a few feet above sea level, and the ground stays wet. Many neighborhoods were built on drained farmland and woods near the swamp, with ditches and ponds to carry rain away. When a slow storm drops several inches, those ditches fill and water spreads into yards, garages and crawl spaces. In October 2016, Hurricane Matthew's heavy rain flooded roads and homes across the city.

Three in four Chesapeake homes are owner-occupied, and most were built after 1980. That means fewer old pipes but plenty of 30-year-old roofs, water heaters and supply lines. Tidal flooding is a growing risk near the branches of the Elizabeth River, and nor'easters can push water up those rivers for days. Humid summers keep crawl spaces damp, and mold follows any leak that is not dried fast.

problems: Low areas in Deep Creek, South Norfolk
Homes near the swamp and river branches
Crawl space drying and mold control
1980s and 1990s homes in Great Bridge, Greenbrier
tips: Keep roadside ditches and yard drains clear of debris.
Buy flood insurance early; it usually takes 30 days to start.
Add a vapor barrier and keep crawl space vents working.
Replace a water heater that is 10 to 12 years old.
areas: Calls come from Great Bridge, Greenbrier, Deep Creek, Western Branch, Hickory, South Norfolk, Indian River and Grassfield, plus Norfolk, Portsmouth and Suffolk.

faq.q: Why does my Chesapeake yard flood after every big rain?
faq.a: Much of the city is flat and low, with a high water table. Rain drains through ditches and ponds, and when they fill, water has nowhere to go. Clear ditches, keep downspouts pointed away from the house and grade soil away from the foundation. A flood policy covers water that comes in from outside.
